To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The FDTD method can accurately estimate the MIMO channel matrix of generic wireless massive MIMO systems, and 2) Passive structures can manipulate the MIMO channel structure, as evidenced by changes in the dominant eigensystem.

the FDTD computational paradigm provides a reliable and computationally efficient method of estimating the channel matrix of massive MIMO systems, and that engineered frequency selective surfaces can be utilized to modify the dominant eigenspaces of the channel matrix.
the FDTD method can accurately model the massive MIMO channel, and that the FDTD model can be used to design and optimize passive frequency selective surfaces for the massive MIMO systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient computational paradigms for the analysis of the channel matrix of massive MIMO systems.
the development of a novel, rigorous, and efficient computational framework for the analysis of massive MIMO systems in realistic scenarios.
the development of a rigorous EM analysis of wireless MIMO systems, with a particular focus on massive MIMO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented work demonstrates the importance of the synergy between stochastic communication theories and rigorous EM analysis for emerging wireless technologies (e.g., 5G and beyond), and the need for further research in this area.

the proposed FDTD computational paradigm, which is based on a rigorous EM analysis, is a very efficient method to estimate the channel matrices of generic massive MIMO systems, and it is capable of capturing the effect of the mutual coupling between the BS elements, as well as the impact of the spherical wavefront illumination.
this letter demonstrates the advantage in using rigorous EM analysis and statistical communication techniques, with applications in emerging wireless technology (e.g., 5G and beyond).

we have demonstrated that the wireless channel properties can be manipulated through the EM wave propagation characteristics.
